Hi all — technical checklist and rationale below. I've attached the CSV with the canonical IPs and a small runbook diff describing the outbound probe we use for validation (runbook-diff.txt).

Attachments: egress-ip-list.csv, runbook-diff.txt

Overview / decision model
- Primary offering: customer-dedicated NAT IPs (static) bound to your private connector. These are the simplest for strict allowlist policies.
- Optional: ephemeral pool with 30d rotation that we can push to customers who accept periodic updates. Ephemeral is only recommended when customers cannot manage static assignments.

Firewall rules (required)
- Outbound IPs: 3 addresses (listed in attached CSV) — allow TCP/443 outbound to these IPs. We recommend only permitting the 3 addresses to limit blast radius.
- Ports: 443 for API/control plane. If you operate an egress proxy that does TLS inspection, allow CONNECT on 443. No other ports required.
- DNS: allow resolution to redwood-inference-hosted domains (we provide an internal CNAME; see attached). If you cannot allow FQDNs, the three IPs are sufficient.

TLS & authentication
- Control plane -> connector: mutual TLS is enforced for control plane operations (port 443). Redwood will present a client cert; your connector should require mTLS for API calls coming from our IPs.- TLS version: TLS 1.3 required.
- SNI: we support SNI pinning; if you operate SNI-based inspection, expect our SNI to be proxy.redwood-inference.com.

Operational controls & rotation
- Static IP option: no rotation unless requested (recommended for strict allowlists).
- Ephemeral option: max rotation window = 30 days; Redwood will post a 48-hour advance notice and provide deterministic mapping (CSV).
- Emergency rotation: in case of key compromise or incident, we will notify and schedule rotation with a 2-hour SLA for notification and 24h for cutover.

Validation & evidence required for signoff
- After you add the three IPs to the firewall, Redwood will initiate 24h of TLS handshakes and a short synthetic request every 5 minutes. For signoff please share a 24h firewall trace that shows successful outbound TLS to one of the listed IPs (we just need source/dest IP, port, timestamp).
- For SOC2/compliance requests we can provide our control-plane certificate chain and a signed SWE attestation for the connector model.

Fallback behavior
- If an IP is blocked or unreachable, requests automatically fall back to a hosted routing path (hosted API endpoint) for 60s while we attempt reconnect; this preserves availability but will change the origin IP and may break IP-only allowlists.

Notes / constraints
- We do not recommend broad port openings (e.g., 80, 443 to entire CIDR) — please scope to the three IPs.
- If your ops team requires DNS-based allowlisting only, confirm and we'll send the CNAME and fingerprint list instead of IPs.

Action items
- Marissa: confirm whether Novacorp prefers Static or Ephemeral (reply here).
- Tom: share the preferred maintenance window for firewall changes (ETA).
- Laura/Ben: I'll need a short approval ticket in JIRA (INF-412) to attach the runbook.

Cheers,
